title: The absolute truth
prompt:
The starter reads one signed number into the value register. Print its magnitude: `-42` prints as `42`.

Compare the register against zero, skip the sign flip when it is already positive, and flip it otherwise. `neg` produces the negation of a register in one instruction.

## what is checked

- the magnitude is printed on its own line
- the program exits cleanly
- a comparison decides, and the sign flip uses `neg`
- the same holds for other inputs you do not see: positive values and zero have to come out unchanged
starter:
// print the absolute value of a signed number
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(value_r, x19)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld"
fmt_out:    .string "magnitude = %lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
value_m:    .skip 8

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read the value
        ldr     x1, =value_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =value_m
        ldr     value_r, [x9]

        // TODO: if value_r is negative, flip its sign so the
        // printf below prints the magnitude

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     x1, value_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
